data.body_html:
August 2040 in Marbella means long, sun-drenched days, warm Mediterranean waters, and the peak of the charter season. If you’re planning a Marbella boat rental weather August 2040 is your key to a perfect day on the water. This guide covers sea temperatures, wind patterns, and insider tips for making the most of your charter from Puerto Banús.

August Weather Snapshot for Marbella

August delivers consistent high pressure over the Costa del Sol. Expect air temperatures between 30°C and 34°C, with sea surface temperatures averaging 26°C — ideal for swimming. The prevailing wind is the Poniente (west wind), typically 10–15 knots, which builds around midday and fades by 17:00. Visibility ranges from 10 to 12 nautical miles, offering clear views of the African coast on good days. UV index hits 9–10, so sun protection is non-negotiable.

Best Times to Charter in August

Morning charters (10:00–14:00) offer flat seas and cooler temperatures. Afternoon trips (16:00–20:00) catch the golden hour and calmer winds. For a full day, an 8-hour charter from 10:00 to 18:00 is popular — you’ll cover more coastline and enjoy a lunch stop. Our boat rental in Marbella fleet includes shaded flybridges and air-conditioned cabins on models like the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Mangusta 80.

What to Expect: Sea Conditions & Swimming

With sea temps at 26°C, you can swim comfortably for hours. Popular anchorages include Cala Cortés (sheltered cove), Cabopino (sandbar and dunes), and the cliffs near Cala del Faro. The Poniente wind can create a light chop on open water, but our skippers know the lee shores. All charters include swim ladders, towels, and safety gear.

Which Boat for August Heat?

For groups of up to 12, the Mangusta 80 (24m) offers a spacious shaded deck and a free jet ski — perfect for cooling off. The Ferretti 94 (29m) provides luxurious air-conditioned saloons. For couples or small families, the Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) is nimble and affordable. See our full fleet page for specs and pricing.

Pricing & Booking Tips for August 2040

  • Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39): €749/2h → €2,299/8h (skipper, drinks, VAT included).
  • Mangusta 80 (white or grey): €4,719 minimum 4h (includes free jet ski).
  • Other boats: pricing on request via WhatsApp.
  • Book 4–6 weeks ahead; August slots fill fast.

What’s Included in Every Charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden fees. You just bring sunscreen and a good attitude.

Local Spots to Visit in August

Head west to Estepona (8 NM) for its colourful old town and marina. East, Cabopino (5 NM) offers a naturist beach and dune reserve. For a longer cruise, Sotogrande (20 NM) is a luxury port with fine dining. Your skipper will tailor the route to your preferences.
